summary: Adds useful point or vertex attributes for line-strip context, including displacement, distance, direction to next or previous vertices, tangent, curvature, angle per distance, and line-strip identity.

key_concepts: Line Metrics converts line-strip topology into attributes such as displacement, distance, direction, tangent, curvature, and angle-per-distance.
Start/end distance and normalized distance attributes are useful lookup coordinates for gradients, widths, effects, and resampling workflows.
Continuous Direction and neighbor controls help keep direction-style attributes stable when line strips contain coincident points.
common_gotchas: Use Continuous Direction when duplicate or coincident points would otherwise produce unstable direction vectors.
Metrics depend on line-strip topology; run Line Break or Primitive first if the input is only loose points.
Distance and tangent attributes are excellent inputs for Lookup, Math Mix, and Line Smooth stages.
